title: SQL Injection - Login Authentication Bypass
payload_used: Email: ' OR 1=1 -- ; password: arbitrary value (reported successful in this lab)
impact: An attacker may bypass authentication and access an account without knowing its password. If the affected account is an administrator, this can expose or allow modification of application data and settings.
remediation: Use parameterized queries/prepared statements; verify passwords using a secure password-hashing function; avoid building SQL statements through string concatenation; apply least-privilege database permissions.

title: SQL Injection - Product Search
payload_used: To be recorded after the search injection is successfully tested; do not treat the normal 'apple' search as exploit evidence.
impact: If the search input is concatenated into a SQL query, an attacker may alter the query and retrieve or manipulate data beyond the intended product search, depending on database permissions and query structure.
remediation: Use parameterized queries for the search term; validate input as appropriate; restrict database account permissions; avoid exposing database errors to users.

title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
url_or_endpoint: Search or other request parameter that is reflected in the response (record the exact URL/parameter after testing)
mitre_attack: T1059.007 - JavaScript (related execution behavior; not a one-to-one XSS classification)
payload_used: To be recorded after the reflected XSS test is successfully reproduced.
impact: An attacker may craft a link that causes script to execute in a victim's browser when the victim opens the link, potentially allowing actions or access within the victim's application session.
remediation: Contextually encode untrusted data before placing it in HTML; sanitize allowed HTML with a maintained allowlist sanitizer; avoid unsafe DOM insertion; use Content Security Policy as defense in depth.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
url_or_endpoint: Product review/comment submission and display location (confirm the exact route or page during testing)
mitre_attack: T1059.007 - JavaScript (related execution behavior; not a one-to-one XSS classification)
payload_used: To be recorded after a harmless test payload is stored and shown to execute when the saved content is viewed again.
impact: A script saved in application content may execute for every user who views the affected content, potentially enabling session-related actions or data exposure in the victim's browser.
remediation: Sanitize user-submitted rich text with a strict allowlist; contextually encode output whenever displaying stored data; avoid unsafe DOM insertion; apply Content Security Policy as defense in depth.
